output.summary: I checked all 17 tests (15 green, 2 red) against the engine's area-of-effect code at `dungdra/spells.py:1132`. Each test was run against at least one deliberate break of the rule, applied in a scratch copy. Breaks covered: always judging cover from the caster; judging cover from the point the area is aimed at; judging it from some other point; removing the Total Cover exclusion; letting Half, Three-Quarters or any cover block the area; and excluding everyone. Every test failed under the breaks aimed at it. I ran both red tests with `--runxfail`, and each fails exactly where its ticket says: the log entry reads `rule='GLOSS.area-of-effect'` with no `#3`, and the walled-off hay still catches fire. The rulebook reading looks right in every test: a line is blocked only by Total Cover (clause #4), cover is judged from the point of origin rather than the caster (#1/#2), and a creature in the way gives only Half Cover (ruling R-09). I'm refuting one test as a duplicate. `test_an_areas_lines_are_judged_from_its_point_of_origin` is a line-for-line copy of the existing `test_a_sphere_doesnt_reach_a_creature_behind_total_cover_from_its_origin` (`test_glossary.py:1753`): same Sleep cast at (30,0), same OPEN/WALLED goblins, same cover entry, dice and assertions. `test_a_creature_cut_off_from_the_origin_rolls_no_save_and_takes_nothing` overlaps with the existing `test_total_cover_doesnt_refuse_an_area_spell` (which tests the Cover rule's clause #9), but it also checks that no save is rolled, the name in the log entry and the page number, so I kept it.

verdicts.reason: Exact duplicate of the existing test_a_sphere_doesnt_reach_a_creature_behind_total_cover_from_its_origin (test_glossary.py:1753, GLOSS.sphere#1): same caster, goblins at (25,0)/(35,0), the same total-cover entry from (30,0), forced d20=[1] and identical assertions. Only the marker and comment differ. The test itself is sound (it fails when cover is judged from the caster), but it adds nothing.
